text:
In that corner where we slept together

so many nights, now I have sat down

to walk. The bed of the dead bride and groom

was taken away, or perhaps who knows what happened.


You came early on other business,

and now you are not here. It is the corner

where beside you, one night, I read,

among your tender points,

a tale by Daudet. It is the beloved

corner. Do not mistake it.


I have begun remembering the vanished

summer days, your coming and going,

scant and full and pale through the rooms.


On this rainy night,

now far from both of us two, I suddenly leap...

There are two doors opening closing,

two doors that go and come in the wind,

shadow                      to                      shadow.

translation.title: Trilce: Poem XV - In That Corner Where We Slept Together
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the impossible action of sitting down to walk and the final spaced shadow-to-shadow doors.
